feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: 3 children, teacher killed in shooting at Oregon elementary school
entry.summary: Three children and a teacher were killed in a shooting at a Bend, Oregon, elementary school Thursday. Officials say a bystander confronted and fatally shot the 16-year-old suspected shooter.

entry.title: Former mayor of Bend, Oregon, on the deadly shooting at an elementary school
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks to Jeff Eager, former mayor of Bend, Oregon, about the elementary school shooting in his neighborhood.

entry.title: Security expert discusses deadly Oregon school shooting
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep asks security expert Juliette Kayyem of Harvard's Kennedy School about the shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon.

entry.title: Do Americans own the president's papers? Appeals court to weigh in
entry.summary: The administration says papers created in the White House belong to Donald Trump, not to the American people. The case could ultimately end up at the conservative-leaning Supreme Court.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: Three children and a teacher were killed in a shooting at an Oregon school, how Russia is viewing Ukraine's strikes and its growing rift with the U.S., DOJ sues California over its voter rolls.

entry.title: Milwaukee Brewers reach the World Series for the first time in over 40 years
entry.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers are headed to the World Series for the first time since 1982. The Brewers swept the Los Angeles Dodgers, the two-time defending World Series champion.

entry.title: Irish rock band Fontaines D.C. on their new album and remaining true to themselves
entry.summary: The Irish band Fontaines D.C. builds on their global success with the new album "Dopamine Chamber," which a band member describes as the soundtrack to our "glorious age of distraction."

entry.title: Trump cancels public execution, but a line may already have been crossed
entry.summary: President Trump has canceled the livestreaming of the execution of the man behind the attack at Fort Hood in 2009. Some say the public proposal itself - from a Cabinet member - changes norms.

entry.title: Florida Republican Salazar faces growing divide in her Latino-majority district
entry.summary: Republican María Elvira Salazar faces a tough contest in her Miami-area congressional district, with many voters upset about President Trump's immigration policies.

entry.title: Investigation details who donated to the White House ballroom project
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with Washington Post investigative reporter Sarah Blaskey about new documents obtained by the Post that detail donors to the White House ballroom project.
